info.desc: Pinkerton is the second studio album by American alternative rock band Weezer, released on September 24, 1996 on DGC Records. Pinkerton was seen as a departure from the band's original power pop style, replacing it with a darker, more abrasive sound with themes drawn from songwriter Rivers Cuomo's disillusionment with the rock lifestyle. It was the last Weezer album to feature bassist Matt Sharp. Initially a commercial and critical failure, Pinkerton went on to achieve cult status and wide acclaim years after its release. .

podcast.body: After the band's second album did not perform as well as hoped, frontman Rivers Cuomo reacted by dropping out of Harvard, where he had been studying music. He then isolated himself in a room with black-painted walls and ceilings, and windows blacked out with fiberglass insulation, as part of a plan to eliminate weaknesses and focus on writing the perfect pop song. "When Weezer's second album, Pinkerton, didn't do as well as Rivers Quomo had hoped, he dropped out of Harvard where he had been studying music and hid in his room, which are the walls and ceilings painted black and had the windows blacked out with layers of fiberglass insulation."

podcast.body: Released on September 24th, 1996, about two and a half years after the Blue Album, this record had high expectations but delivered a darker, self-produced sound, reflecting Rivers Cuomo's disillusionment with the rock star lifestyle and his painful leg surgery. It was only 34 minutes long, composed of material left over from Rivers' abandoned rock opera project "Songs From the Black Hole," and covered themes of former girlfriends, groupies, fan letters, and a search for identity. The album was considered a "proto-emo" record, ahead of its time, and initially sold less than one million copies, facing a restraining order from Pinkerton Inc. over its title. "It was, if anything, a proto-emal record, something that people weren't quite ready for in 1996."

podcast.body: This 1996 album was salvaged from the aborted *Songs from the Black Hole* project, mixing its surviving concepts (love, groupies, fans, personal identity) with elements of Puccini's 1904 opera *Madama Butterfly*. The name comes from B.F. Pinkerton, a main character in the opera, which Rivers was exposed to while studying music composition at Harvard. The album, ultimately a concept record, explores themes of lost love, sexual loneliness, and frustration. Written entirely in the first person, it comes across as an autobiography of Rivers Cuomo's life. "Adding his space opera to the Puccini Opera resulted in an album called Pinkerton in 1996."

podcast.body: This album was released in 1996, marking the beginning of a hiatus for Weezer. The band's 2000 Warped Tour appearance occurred near the end of this hiatus, before their _Green Album_ was released. "that was right near the end of the hiatus between the Pinkerton album which came out in 1996, and just before the Green album in 2001."

podcast.body: This was Weezer's second album, released in 1996, and it was with this record that the "emo" label truly began to stick to the band. Emo fans specifically gravitated towards the emotional and confessional lyrical style emanating from singer Rivers Cuomo's introspective mindset. "But the label really started to stick with the second album, Pinkerton. Again, emo fans gravitated to River's Cuomo's headspace."

podcast.body: This was the band's second album, originally released in 1996. By 2010, when Death to False Metal was released, Pinkerton was finally receiving the recognition and praise that had eluded it upon its initial release. Its re-issue coincided with the release of Death to False Metal. "Pinkerton, of course, being the second album. And by now, Pinkerton was getting the recognition and praise that escaped it when it was first released in 1996."

podcast.body: Weezer's "Pinkerton" album emerged from the abandoned "Songs From The Black Hole" project. Although the original space opera concept was dropped, many fans consider "Pinkerton" to feature some of Weezer's best work, showcasing how elements of the lost album found new life. "However, Songs From The Black Hole lives on. The project morphed into the Pinkerton album which many fans now agree features some of Weezer's best work."

podcast.body: Weezer's 1996 album "Pinkerton" is regarded as a significant influence on the emo genre, particularly as emo began to gain mainstream traction towards the end of the 1990s. "Weasers Pinkerton album was seen as a big influence."
